name_reason: Conforms to fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>; the descriptor accurately captures the function's role: it seeds (init) the pathfind state globals and the origin tile marker, then kicks off the movement-range flood fill. No address residue, no generic placeholder. The plate also calls it an 'orchestrator'; 'init' covers the seeding/setup role well. Distinct from the path-aware sibling fd2_pathfind_to_destination and from the recursive helper fd2_flood_fill_movement_range_recursive.
purpose: Movement-range flood-fill orchestrator: seeds the pathfind state globals from the caller's six arguments, marks the origin tile with the full step budget, and kicks off the recursive 4-neighbour expansion that paints the 'where can this unit move?' markers.
logic_summary: Spills all six __cdecl stack args into the pathfind state globals at 0x60060..0x60070 (caller_context/secondary cost table first, then seed_x/seed_y/max_steps, the tile-map pointer, and the primary tile-attribute cost-table pointer). Reads map_width from tile_map[0] and map_height from tile_map[2]. Computes the origin tile's marker pointer = tile_map + ((uint16)(map_width*seed_y)+seed_x)*4 + 7 and writes max_steps there as the starting (highest) residual cost. Then calls fd2_flood_fill_movement_range_recursive(seed_x, seed_y, max_steps, origin_ptr); in the binary the recursion inherits the secondary cost-table base via ESI (captured into caller_context) and the map_width*4 row stride via EBP (recomputed inside the helper from the map_width global). EAX is never read by any of the 6 call sites (all do ADD ESP,0x18), so it is effectively void.
signature: void fd2_init_movement_range_floodfill(uint32 ct, uint32 x, uint32 y, uint32 rng, uint32 tm, uint32 af)

params.name: ct
params.semantics: Caller context / secondary cost-table base: the per-job movement-cost table the caller obtained from fd2_get_movement_cost_table_for_job. Stored 32-bit into data_fd2_battle_pathfind_caller_context (binary's ESI capture, first store); the leaf step reads it back as the cost table indexed by the primary table's secondary index.
params.reason: Short domain abbreviation (cost table) matching the caller's source variable (pMove_cost_table); not a generic placeholder, no address residue, and fully documented in the comment block. Terse but functional.

params.name: x
params.semantics: Origin tile X (source column); truncated to its low byte into data_fd2_battle_pathfind_floodfill_seed_x. Caller passes cursor_world_x.
params.reason: Clear coordinate name matching its use as the origin column; no address residue.

params.name: y
params.semantics: Origin tile Y (source row); truncated to its low byte into data_fd2_battle_pathfind_floodfill_seed_y. Caller passes cursor_world_y.
params.reason: Clear coordinate name matching its use as the origin row; no address residue.

params.name: rng
params.semantics: Movement step budget (range); truncated to its low byte into data_fd2_battle_pathfind_floodfill_max_steps and written into the origin tile's marker as the starting (highest) residual cost. Caller passes range_remaining.
params.reason: Clear abbreviation (range) matching its use as the step budget; no address residue.

params.name: tm
params.semantics: Battle tile map base (4-byte-per-tile map); stored 32-bit into data_fd2_battle_pathfind_battle_tile_map_ptr and used as the base for origin-tile address math. map_width = tm[0], map_height = tm[2].
params.reason: Clear abbreviation (tile map) matching its use; no address residue.

params.name: af
params.semantics: Primary tile-attribute -> cost lookup table base; stored 32-bit into data_fd2_battle_pathfind_tile_cost_table_ptr. The leaf step indexes it at [(attr & 0x3FF)<<2 + 1] to obtain the secondary index into the per-job cost table (ct). Caller passes tile_attribute_flags_buffer_ptr.
params.reason: Short abbreviation (attribute flags) matching the caller's source variable (tile_attribute_flags_buffer_ptr); not a generic placeholder, no address residue, fully documented. Terse but functional.

returns.semantics: No meaningful return. The decompiled 'return in_EAX' is a pass-through signature artifact; all 6 call sites do ADD ESP,0x18 and discard EAX, so the function is effectively void.
